extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in creativity; writers and comedians looking for craft insight
extracted.subtask_description: A short blog post/interview excerpt presenting a comedian's formative lesson about creative writing and related reader comments that offer craft observations. Useful as informal guidance for humor writers and performers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the ordinary extraordinary
rubrics_metrics.description: Phrase attributed to Ricky Gervais (via reader comment): 'making the ordinary extraordinary.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elevate everyday experiences in your writing/performances; find interest and universality in ordinary detail. The comment adds that 'honesty sells' and that a particularly effective final minute of Gervais's anecdote was replayed by the reader, suggesting concrete, honest detail makes material memorable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty/authenticity in material
rubrics_metrics.description: Reader summary: 'Honesty sells.' Another comment referencing Keith Johnstone emphasizes being 'obvious and average' because that is when you are your most unique and creative—it's actually YOU, not an imitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize material that is true to your own experience and voice rather than trying to copy trends or other performers. Authentic, simple truths can feel original and resonate more than forced cleverness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use obviousness/averageness as a creative route
rubrics_metrics.description: Paraphrase of Keith Johnstone in comments: being obvious and average in your creativity is valuable because it reveals your individuality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow yourself to start from commonplace, straightforward observations; this can lead to distinctive perspectives. Avoid over-polishing or trying to appear clever at the cost of losing personal authenticity.
